name: Differential equations
description: Equations that predict how machines, tanks, populations and springs change over time, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Differential equations realm ("Differential equations"): equations that say how something changes, and how to predict
what it does next, for an adult who has finished Foundations, Calculus 1, Calculus 2 and Linear algebra. Same Kepler
outpost, now with machines that run themselves, and Mira is still the mentor. The concept plan is docs/plans/ODE-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Equations of change
chapters.blurb: What a differential equation is, how to read one, and the first ways to solve one.

sector.purpose: drive machines without shaking them apart

chapters.name: Systems
chapters.blurb: Systems x′ = Ax solved with eigenvalues, and pictures of their trajectories.

sector.name: Control Room
sector.purpose: run several linked machines at once

chapters.name: The Laplace transform
chapters.blurb: Turning differential equations into algebra, for switches and impulses.

chapters.name: Beyond the formulas
chapters.blurb: Series solutions, nonlinear systems near equilibrium, and boundary value problems.

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Nothing here stays put any more, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have the derivatives, integrals and matrices from the earlier realms. I’ll go through the worked example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
The machines run themselves.
Learn to predict what they do next.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome back. The outpost's machines now react to each other: tanks drain, springs bounce, populations rise and fall. An equation that says how something changes can tell us where it is going, and we start with the greenhouse seedlings.
copy.allDone: You did it. Every machine, tank and population at the outpost is predicted, and you know when one will settle or swing. Waves comes next, where the strings and air of the outpost start to ring.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from first-order equations to the Laplace transform. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the result before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Machines that change over time, predicted.
help.intro: Differential equations start from the basics: what an equation that links a quantity to its rate of change means, and how to solve the first kinds. The pack then adds second-order equations for springs, forcing and resonance, systems of equations, the Laplace transform, and nonlinear systems near equilibrium. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Constants, roots, eigenvalues and coefficients are typed as plain numbers, never as a formula; a classification is typed as its code from the question, and complex roots take the real and imaginary parts in two boxes. Angles are in radians and times and lengths in SI units.
